N. S. Bakhvalov 1959 (fooling-function lower bounds for Hoelder classes; classical technique)
comparison.explanation: Shows that the lack of QMC support observed by GKS is a genuine worst-case barrier: on the non-monotone class every deterministic rule (QMC included, adaptive or not) has error >= c_s n^{-1/s} (worse than Monte Carlo for s >= 3), whereas the randomized estimators of R5/R8 achieve n^{-1/2-1/(2s)} and n^{-1/2-1/s} sqrt(log n). The fooling-function technique is classical; its instantiation inside the preintegration class is new.
